note: Butler County Conservation Board campground in Heery Woods State Park (state-owned since 1934, county-managed since 1974) on the Shell Rock River at Clarksville, just above the park's low-head dam. Sites 1-11 are gravel back-ins in a row along the riverbank; 12-19 sit on an inland loop to the east. Boat ramp, canoe access, accessible fishing pier below the dam, trails to the Rolling Prairie Trail. --Claude
summary: Operator confirmed: Butler County Conservation Board (the park is state-owned, county-managed since 1974). Confirmed $20/$25 + $4, 50-amp, showers. Added flush toilets, potable water, no dump (town of Clarksville), water hookup false, booking (sites 7-10 online, 7-day lead, 2-night weekend min, 14-night max), season May 1-Oct 15. Waterfront lead: sites 1-11 line the riverbank, so riverfront rather than not waterfront.
flags: WATERFRONT LEAD not waterfront -> riverfront for sites 1-11: the county's Campground Detail map (park gallery on MyCountyParks) draws sites 1-11 (7-10 the reservable ones) as back-in pads in a row on the Shell Rock River bank, with their spur road on the inland side. The county's site photos show gravel pads with the river directly behind across grass and a few trees. Imagery puts the pads under canopy ~10-20 m from the water at about 42.7676-42.7685,-92.6695 to -92.6685. The river there is the pool above the low-head dam and roughly 100+ m wide. Sites 12-19 and the tent sites are on an inland loop ~100-250 m east, not waterfront. There is no bluff view to speak of: the campground is down on the bank, not on the bluff.

OPERATOR: Butler County Conservation Board. The park page says it was bought by the Iowa Conservation Commission in 1934 and 'has been managed by the Butler County Conservation Board since 1974'. The 'State Park' name is historical, so ownership local stands.
SITES: MyCountyParks lists tent sites T1-T4 only; the county's map labels T1-T6. The count is 25, by the map (the old note's 6 tent sites agrees).
FEES undated: the site pages give $20/$25 + $4 with no year. A 2023 fishing pier is mentioned, so the page is 2023 or later.

HOOKUPS water false is read from 'Fresh water is available to fill reserve tanks' plus the T1 page's 'no permanent hook-ups'. Facilities dump false: the dump station is in the town of Clarksville, not the park.

PIN OK: the stored pin is at the dam/parking lot ~50-100 m from the riverside row and within ~200 m of the east loop. The Google pin (42.77083,-92.66658) is ~400 m NE in the woods by Hwy 188; don't use it.
PHONE: Google lists (319) 278-4237; the county site pages say 'Call for Availability 319-346-6551'. The entry has no phone; suggest 319-346-6551, the county's own number. Website confirmed.
FIT: no rig length posted; the pads are gravel back-ins that look roomy in the county photos.
